evidence_class: response-open historical field-design audit; not a mechanism test

prospective_decision.preferred: same-day TNC coring and fixed-transect baseline survey
prospective_decision.rule: Do not rely on historical routine survey timing. Coordinate the future baseline fixed-transect survey and TNC campaign as one planned field campaign.
prospective_decision.routine_schedule_fallback: If routine monitoring cannot meet the frozen window, conduct a dedicated additional baseline fixed-transect survey under the same quantitative protocol.
prospective_decision.failure_boundary: Samples whose paired baseline cannot be obtained within +/-14 days under the <=28-day TNC campaign are descriptive-only; do not widen the seasonal window.

interpretation: Historical routine Tampa monitoring timing is too dispersed to support the planned confirmatory TNC design as a passive add-on. A synchronized baseline survey must be planned with the TNC campaign.
claim_boundary: Historical timing is a logistics audit, not ecological evidence.
The 28-day campaign and +/-14-day baseline-alignment rules were not relaxed after inspection.
Do not choose the historical densest window as the prospective season because it maximizes sample count.
No future biological response is opened.
